native_scope_limit: Package version and checksum equality does not establish resolved features, all transitive dependencies, toolchain execution or runtime behavior. current_source_observations.observation: The endpoint-origin delta is passed to Dir3::new; every rejection returns successful fraction 1 and no hit before the shape cast. The pinned Dir3 source computes a norm and requires a finite positive result; a rejected nonzero segment is therefore not distinguished here from an exact-zero clear path. Reachability of extreme inputs in supported gameplay is not demonstrated.

Muzzle delta and length are computed separately; Dir3 rejection substitutes camera direction before cast_ray while retaining the muzzle-derived distance. A later checked Position can reject some resulting values; no committed incorrect aim or ordinary runtime witness is asserted.

Soft-occlusion query derives anchor-to-camera delta and length, substitutes NEG_Z on direction rejection, and publishes None when the query returns no hit. No-hit from a valid query is legitimate; the conditional issue is loss of the intended rejected nonzero segment. No supported ordinary failure is claimed.

native_source.qualification: Installed rust-src bytes match the historical citation; the repository pins the same nightly date. No compiler execution or historical build identity is inferred.

current_source_observations.observation: CameraProfile.distance retains SignedLength, whose constructor admits finite negatives. On a new observation the retained boom is initialized from the blended profile and used by sweet_spot_target. If the resulting allowed horizontal or vertical half-window is strictly negative, its clamp bounds are reversed and the pinned f32 clamp source specifies a panic before the CameraResult is returned. For example this condition is possible when a negative distance is combined with positive finite view and screen extents. Signed offsets and zero have separate legitimate roles; this is a camera boom-domain obligation, not a proposed global SignedLength restriction.
current_source_observations.qualification: The default positive profiles do not witness this case. Actual availability of a custom negative configuration and the intended negative or zero modes have not been established; no runtime was probed.

current_source_observations.observation: CloseCameraProfile exposes two independently admitted signed endpoints. When start, full and sampled distance coincide, blend computes 0/0, and the cited f32 clamp preserves NaN when bounds are 0 and 1. The NaN is passed into affine composition; the endpoint then admits its resulting position through a finite-component check. The default endpoints 1.8 and 0.65 are distinct.
current_source_observations.qualification: The supported policy for equal or reversed custom endpoints and reachability of the exact sample remain open. This source trace does not claim a default-config failure or runtime behavior.

current_source_observations.observation: Rig and aim state are singleton resources, while their systems iterate a relation-camera query. The shown normal presentation setup spawns one marked gameplay camera, and the local-player hook requires a Single marked camera before attaching its controller relation. With multiple relation cameras, the shared state is advanced or cleared in each iteration; that is a population policy question rather than evidence of a normal multi-camera failure.
current_source_observations.qualification: No claim that unrelated render cameras have the relation or that multi-camera use is supported or occurs. Historical broad suspicion remains rejected within the original stated scope; custom population policy and other setup paths are open.

current_source_observations.observation: Placement stages a copy of boom recovery, performs the final sweep and checked position admission, then commits recovery. Rig observation uses a cloned or reset history and commits that history and camera translation only after prepare returns Ok. The separate profile blend is advanced before preparation and may already have changed on a later error.
current_source_observations.qualification: This supports the historical rejection of a broad unstaged pose-publication suspicion, not a guarantee that every camera state field is unchanged on error. A rejected nonzero sweep direction currently returning success remains the distinct proposal 4 issue; staging alone does not prove a valid sweep.

current_source_observations.observation: The cited Avian ShapeCastConfig::from_max_distance stores its argument directly and its default uses Scalar::MAX; application segment identity is not established by that constructor. The inspected shape-cast candidate code skips both a Parry error and a no-hit result through the same branch, and its public result is Option<ShapeHitData>; another candidate may still yield a hit. The ray entry point also returns Option. Whether the application needs a separate cause or different segment bound is an open policy question.
